title: Keep a mutable object in a constant binding
summary: Keep the object identity while updating its visit count.
rules: const prevents rebinding, not object mutation.
let and const have block scope and cannot be accessed before initialization.

title: Normalize a numeric form field before comparison
summary: Reject blank and nonnumeric input explicitly, then compare numbers.
rules: Strict equality does not coerce different operand types.
Number of an empty string is zero; validate empty input before conversion.

title: Update a profile without mutating the original
summary: Create a shallow copy with a normalized name. Nested objects still share identity.
syntax:
const object = { key: value, method() {} };
const copy = { ...object, key: replacement };
rules: Object spread copies own enumerable properties shallowly.
Later properties overwrite earlier ones.

title: Separate a task title from its remaining fields
summary: Extract a display value while keeping the other task fields.
syntax:
const { key: local = fallback, ...rest } = object;
const [first, ...remaining] = array;
rules: Defaults apply to undefined, not null.
Rest collects remaining fields or items.

title: Find active task names in a stable order
summary: Filter completed tasks before transforming the remaining items.
rules: map transforms each item; filter selects items.
Supply an initial accumulator to reduce, including for empty arrays.

title: Skip inactive work and stop at a limit
summary: Select at most the requested number of unfinished tasks.
syntax:
if (condition) { statement; } else { statement; }
for (const item of iterable) { statement; }
rules: for...of iterates values; for...in iterates enumerable property keys.
break ends the loop; continue skips its current iteration.

title: Create independent counters with captured state
summary: Each call owns a different count binding.
rules: A closure retains access to lexical bindings after its outer call returns.
Arrow functions inherit this; ordinary functions receive this from their call site.

title: Export a reusable text helper
summary: Import slug from this module; no TypeScript compiler is required.
rules: Named imports use exported names; default imports choose a local name.
Node treats .js as ESM with package type module; .mjs is always ESM.

title: Display an optional profile name
summary: Use the fallback only when the profile or its name is missing.
rules: Optional chaining stops at null or undefined.
Nullish coalescing preserves zero, false and empty strings.

title: Collect successful async results and report failures
summary: Capture synchronous throws from loaders as well as promise rejections.
rules: An async function returns a promise; throws reject it.
all rejects on a failure; allSettled waits for every outcome.

title: Return a useful error when JSON is invalid
summary: Preserve the cause while exposing a task-specific message.
syntax: try { operation(); } catch (error) { recover(error); } finally { cleanup(); }
rules: Throw Error objects to retain a message and stack.
finally runs after success or failure; returning from finally overrides prior results.

title: Format a task using a template expression
summary: Interpolate an expression without concatenation. Use textContent when displaying untrusted text.
rules: Expressions inside ${...} execute as JavaScript.
Template literals preserve literal newlines and do not escape HTML.

title: Count task categories with a Map
summary: Accumulate counts without object prototype-key collisions.
rules: Map keys may be any value and retain insertion order.
Map.get returns undefined for an absent key; has distinguishes stored undefined.

title: Encapsulate a balance with a private class field
summary: Validate deposits before changing private state.
rules: Private fields can only be accessed inside their declaring class.
Methods receive this from the call site; pass a closure when preserving an instance.

title: Attach a click handler and remove it later
summary: Return a cleanup function so the caller can stop observing clicks.
rules: Removal requires the same callback identity and capture setting.
textContent inserts text without interpreting HTML.

title: Cancel a pending JSON request
summary: The caller owns cancellation and must handle result rejection, including AbortError.
rules: fetch rejects on network errors and aborts, not HTTP error statuses.
Check response.ok and pass the signal to fetch; each controller cancels once.

title: Read a UTF-8 file in Node
summary: Read a caller-provided local file; no hardcoded path or external service.
rules: An encoding returns text; omitting it returns a Buffer.
Await filesystem promises and handle failures such as ENOENT.

title: Render a component with props and children
summary: Compose a panel with supplied content rather than calling the component as a normal function.
syntax:
function Component({ label, children }) { return <section>{label}{children}</section>; }
<Component label="Title">content</Component>
rules: Capitalize component names and pass props as attributes.
Children are content nested inside a component; JSX expressions use braces.

title: Read an input from a change handler
summary: Keep input state controlled and type the extracted event handler in TSX.
syntax:
<button onClick={handler}>label</button>
<input onChange={event => read(event.currentTarget.value)} />
rules: Pass a handler function rather than invoking it during render.
currentTarget is the element with the handler; target may be a nested element.

title: Count clicks with a functional state update
summary: Queue an update based on the previous count, with an optional typed label in TSX.
syntax:
const [value, setValue] = useState(initial);
setValue(previous => next);
rules: Call hooks unconditionally at the top level of a component or custom hook.
Use a functional update when the next value depends on the previous state.

title: Render keyed tasks with a conditional empty state
summary: Use fragments, expressions, stable keys and a visible empty state.
syntax:
{items.length ? items.map(item =>
  • {item.name}
    • ) :

    empty

    }
rules: Keys identify siblings across updates; prefer stable IDs over array positions.
Use a boolean condition or ternary; zero with && can render a visible zero.

title: Subscribe to window events with effect cleanup
summary: Subscribe once, remove the same handler on cleanup, and render the measured width.
rules: Effects synchronize with external systems after commit.
Cleanup runs before an effect restarts and on unmount; development StrictMode probes setup and cleanup.

title: Abort a stale request when a component changes
summary: Handle HTTP errors and cancellation without allowing an old request to replace the new result.
rules: Keep the effect callback synchronous and start async work inside it.
Abort obsolete work on cleanup and ignore its outcome before updating state.

title: Focus an input through a DOM ref
summary: Guard the nullable element reference and specify its DOM type in TSX.
rules: Refs persist across renders and changing them does not rerender.
A DOM ref is null before mounting and after unmounting.

title: Validate JSON before accepting a task
summary: Express 5: export the app for local request tests; listen only in the launcher.
rules: Install JSON middleware before routes that consume JSON.
Request bodies are untrusted; validate shape and values.

title: Handle a rejected Express route in error middleware
summary: Keep private error details out of the response; Express 4 requires explicit async forwarding.
rules: Express 5 forwards rejected route promises automatically.
Error middleware has four parameters and goes after routes; delegate when headers are sent.

title: Test a synchronous result and async rejection
summary: Run this file through Vitest; it registers a test rather than executing on import.
rules: Await promise assertions so failures belong to the test.
Test observable behavior and isolate local state between tests.

title: Test a React interaction through its accessible role
summary: Use a DOM test environment (jsdom), React and Testing Library with Vitest.
rules: Query the UI by accessible role and name.
Await user interactions and clean up mounted trees after each test.

title: Function forms and parameters
summary: Choose hoisted declarations or assigned functions; make omitted arguments explicit.
rules: Declarations are initialized before execution in their scope; assigned expressions wait for initialization.
Default parameters apply to undefined, not null. Rest is a real array and must be last.
Arrow functions capture this and arguments from their enclosing scope.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Receivers and callback binding
summary: A regular function receives this from its call site; bind fixes it for later calls.
rules: Extracting a method loses its receiver in strict ESM. Event listeners receive the event target as this.
call/apply invoke immediately; bind returns a new function whose receiver cannot be rebound.
Keep the bound callback identity to remove an event listener.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Object identity and cloning
summary: Spread creates a new outer object while nested references remain shared.
rules: === compares object identity; equal-looking objects may be different references.
Spread omits non-enumerable properties and the prototype; structuredClone supports cycles but cannot clone functions.
structuredClone is a data clone, not preservation of class methods or property descriptors.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Prototype lookup and own properties
summary: Inherited properties participate in lookup but need not appear in own-property enumeration.
rules: Object.keys/entries select own enumerable string keys; for...in also sees inherited enumerable keys.
Object.hasOwn works on null-prototype objects and objects that shadow hasOwnProperty.
Use a null-prototype object or Map for untrusted keys, not accidental prototype lookup.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Property descriptors and enumeration
summary: Descriptors control assignment, visibility and redefinition independently.
syntax:
Object.defineProperty(target, key, { value, writable: false, enumerable: false, configurable: false });
Object.defineProperty(target, key, { get() { return value; }, enumerable: true });
rules: Omitted flags default to false in defineProperty, unlike an object literal.
Data descriptors use value/writable; accessors use get/set. Do not combine both forms.
Reflect.ownKeys includes symbols and non-enumerable keys; Object.keys includes only enumerable string keys.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Set membership and deduplication
summary: Sets preserve insertion order and compare keys with SameValueZero.
rules: NaN equals NaN in Set; +0 and -0 share a key. Objects use identity.
Deduplication preserves the first occurrence order. Validate/normalize domain values before adding.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: WeakMap metadata and object identity
summary: Attach metadata without owning the key lifetime or enumerating keys.
rules: WeakMap is not iterable and has no size. Do not use it for a visible cache inventory.
These recipes accept object keys only; cached values are distinguished from cache misses with has.
Garbage collection is nondeterministic; tests assert lookup/invalidation rather than collection timing.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Lazy generators and iterator cleanup
summary: A generator suspends work between yielded values and runs finally on early iterator closure.
rules: Creating a generator does not execute its body. Errors surface when next is called.
Breaking a for...of loop closes the iterator; finally releases resources. Manual next users must close abandoned iterators.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Symbol protocols and iteration
summary: Well-known symbols define interoperable behavior; ordinary symbols create distinct property keys.
rules: Equal descriptions do not make symbols equal. Object.keys ignores symbol keys.
Symbol.iterator returns an iterator with next; a generator method supplies that protocol.
Explicit conversion hooks must return a primitive; invalid hooks throw TypeError.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Regular expressions and captures
summary: Capture structured text, and separate literal search input from pattern syntax.
rules: matchAll requires g for RegExp arguments and returns a lazy iterator. Named groups are accessed via groups.
Use u for Unicode code-point semantics; regex is not a full parser for nested formats.
A reusable g/y regex mutates lastIndex with test/exec; matchAll avoids changing the original lastIndex.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Unicode strings and graphemes
summary: Code units, code points and visible graphemes have different boundaries.
rules: length counts UTF-16 code units; spread counts code points, not user-visible graphemes.
Normalize canonical equivalents before identifier comparison; locale casing is a separate policy.
Segmenter results depend on ICU Unicode data; pin the runtime for reproducibility.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Numeric boundaries and exact integers
summary: Validate finite/safe numbers and use BigInt when integer precision must be exact.
rules: Number uses IEEE-754 binary floating point; decimal fractions may not be exact.
BigInt and Number cannot be mixed in arithmetic; BigInt division truncates toward zero.
JSON.stringify rejects BigInt unless explicitly converted to a domain representation.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: JSON parsing, validation and serialization failures
summary: Parsing establishes syntax, not application validity; serialization also has failure and omission rules.
syntax:
const data = JSON.parse(text);
const text = JSON.stringify(value, replacer, space);
rules: Malformed JSON throws SyntaxError; validate object shape after parsing, including null and arrays.
Cycles and BigInt throw during stringify. Undefined/functions/symbols are omitted in objects; nonfinite numbers become null.
A JSON round trip is not a general-purpose clone.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

references.title: JSON parsing, validation and serialization failures

title: Coordinating promise outcomes
summary: Choose fail-fast aggregation, complete outcome reporting, or first settlement deliberately.
rules: all preserves input order and rejects on the first rejection; it does not cancel remaining work.
allSettled reports status/value or status/reason for every input. Wrap job calls to turn synchronous throws into rejections.
race settles with the first result or failure. An empty race remains pending; losers need explicit cleanup/cancellation.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Microtasks and task ordering
summary: Promise reactions and queueMicrotask callbacks run after the current stack, before later timers.
rules: A zero-delay timer schedules a later task, not an immediate call.
Microtasks drain before the next task; recursively queueing them can starve other work.
Do not infer exact elapsed time from timer delay or assume Node-specific nextTick order in browsers.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Cancellation and owned resource cleanup
summary: Pass a signal through owned work and remove listeners/timers on every settlement.
rules: Abort is cooperative and one-shot. A pre-aborted signal must be checked before starting work.
AbortController does not cancel arbitrary promises; the operation must observe its signal.
Remove abort listeners on success and failure; cancel race losers that your operation owns.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM and modern Chromium; no TypeScript annotations required.

title: Node paths and file URLs
summary: Use URL conversion helpers for module-relative files and explicit path policy for user names.
rules: URL pathname is not a decoded OS path. fileURLToPath handles spaces and platform rules.
resolve normalizes path segments; it is not an authorization or symlink sandbox.
Lexical containment must reject .. and absolute escapes; symbolic links still need a separate policy.
Supported: Node 26.3.0 ESM; these node: APIs do not run in browsers.

title: Browser form submission and validation
summary: Read named form controls on submit and apply domain validation as well as browser constraints.
rules: FormData yields strings or Files; absent names return null. Disabled controls are omitted.
requestSubmit runs validation and submit listeners; form.submit bypasses them.
Browser validation improves UX; validate again on the server. Use textContent for untrusted status messages.
Supported: real Chromium through Playwright 1.62.1; DOM and storage APIs require a document/origin.

title: Storage parsing and unavailable persistence
summary: Storage contains strings and may be missing, malformed, blocked or full.
rules: A missing key returns null. Parse and validate stored values before using them.
Accessing localStorage and writing can throw; catch around the access as well as the operation.
Storage is origin-scoped, synchronous and unsuitable for secrets; this example stores only a display preference.
Supported: real Chromium through Playwright 1.62.1; DOM and storage APIs require a document/origin.

title: Delegated DOM events and teardown
summary: Attach one listener to a stable container and select only contained actionable descendants.
rules: target is the originating element; currentTarget is the listener container. Nested spans often become the target.
Guard non-Element targets and containment; closest may climb outside the intended container.
Remove listeners on teardown. Delegation handles future descendants without adding per-item listeners.
Supported: real Chromium through Playwright 1.62.1; DOM and storage APIs require a document/origin.

title: React reducers and immutable actions
summary: Keep related state transitions in a pure reducer and dispatch minimal actions.
syntax:
const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, initialState);
dispatch({ type: "action", value });
rules: Return new state for changes; returning the same object may skip rendering.
Reducers must be pure; Strict Mode may invoke them twice in development.
Validate domain transitions explicitly; dispatch updates the next render, not the current closure.
Supported: React/React DOM 19.3.1 with the pinned JSX transform.

title: React context boundaries and providers
summary: Read the closest provider and distinguish an optional default from a required boundary.
rules: A context default is static and used only when no matching provider exists.
Providers update consumers when their value changes; keep unrelated state outside broad contexts.
A required-context hook can throw early when a provider is missing.
Supported: React/React DOM 19.3.1 with the pinned JSX transform.

title: Accessible React form validation
summary: Use labels, stable error associations and controlled state for form submission.
syntax:
<label htmlFor={id}>Name</label>
<input id={id} value={value} onChange={handler} aria-describedby={errorId} />
<form onSubmit={handler}>...</form>
rules: preventDefault retains control of submission. Keep controlled values strings.
Associate errors with the input and announce results with status/alert roles.
A client form does not replace server validation; distinguish invalid input and persistence failure.
Supported: React/React DOM 19.3.1 with the pinned JSX transform.

title: Express validation and stable error responses
summary: Validate request data and place a final four-argument error handler after routes.
rules: Express 5 forwards thrown/rejected async handler errors. req.body is untrusted and may be undefined.
Malformed JSON fails before the route. Preserve intentional parser statuses such as 400/413.
Send stable public errors without stack traces; delegate if headers were already sent.
Supported: Express 5.3.0 on Node 26.3.0 ESM.

references.title: Express validation and stable error responses

title: Vitest async and DOM assertions
summary: Await async assertions and restore timers or DOM resources even if an assertion fails.
rules: An unawaited rejection assertion can finish after the test; always await or return it.
Fake timers test timer contracts without wall-clock races; restore them in finally/afterEach.
DOM queries should use accessible roles and names; clean up rendered trees and listeners.
Supported: Vitest 5.0.4, Testing Library React 16.3.0 and jsdom 30.1.2.
